crossRendererSourceFidelity.provenScope: Both runtimes expose identical original pixels through an unscaled natural-size canvas draw and getImageData. Chromium opaque crop pixels equal those original coordinates. The native high-quality nine-argument draw reproduces the saved native crops exactly and changes RGB even at integer one-to-one bounds; its low-quality and smoothing-disabled controls equal the original pixels. Alpha masks and crop geometry match exactly. No cross-runtime RGB byte identity is claimed for the high-quality native crop. Internal decoder buffers and compositor output were not measured.
crossRendererSourceFidelity.colorHandling: Original full canvas RGBA equality rules out an observed source color-profile conversion difference in this comparison.
crossRendererSourceFidelity.premultiplication: The opaque-only difference and unclipped fully opaque native high-quality control exclude alpha premultiplication as the cause of those RGB differences; partial-alpha RGB/premultiplied deltas remain reported separately.

independentSpatialReview.scope: Independent view of both whole-crop RGB heatmaps and the source/Chromium/native-high 96-pixel details; final separate Chromium decode verification remains pending.
independentSpatialReview.observation: RGB differences track internal ink, text and painted contrast transitions throughout both crops. No coherent displacement or extra missing region is visible in these difference and detail views. Alpha byte identity and best zero-displacement measurements are separately recorded by the spatial verifier. Native high-quality draw introduces slight intensity smoothing in the shown source-aligned pixels.
